   230	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
   231	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
   232	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
   233	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   234	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   235	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
   236	    (e : C ≅ C') :
   237	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
   238	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
   239	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
   240	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
   241	
   242	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
   243	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
   244	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   245	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   246	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   247	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
   248	  sorry

   250	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
   251	
   252	/-- Identity coherence. -/
   253	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   254	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   255	    baseChangeIso k k C =
   256	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
   257	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
   258	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
   259	  sorry

   261	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
   262	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   263	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
   264	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   266	    baseChangeIso k M C
   267	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
   268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
   269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
   270	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
   271	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   272	  sorry

spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands (unread inbox for your task, your session's runtime/tokens, other live
runs) — read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,

    10	# Conditional final packaging of divisor representability
    11	
    12	DDR-9.F7 has two logically separate parts: lifting the affine equivalences to arbitrary
    13	tests, and packaging the resulting natural equivalences as a `RepresentableBy` datum.
    14	This file formalizes the second part.  `DivRepGlobalData` records the general-test
    15	pullback, classification map, inverse laws, and naturality.  Its `representableBy`
    16	constructor is the final categorical packaging.
    17	
    18	The affine-to-general lift is intentionally not assumed to exist implicitly: a caller
    19	must provide every field of `DivRepGlobalData`.
    20	-/

    23	set_option quotPrecheck false
    24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    41	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    42	
    43	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    44	  [IsIntegral C.left]
    45	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    46	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    47	  [IsDominant pi]

    49	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    50	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    51	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    52	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))

    65	/-- The exact general-test data needed for the final F7 packaging.  In the intended
    66	construction, `pull` is assembled from the affine forward maps and `classify` by
    67	gluing the affine backward classifiers. -/
    68	structure DivRepGlobalData where
    69	  pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    70	    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
    71	  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    72	    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)

    89	  invFun := D.classify

   137	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv.symm F = D.classify F :=

   140	end DivRepGlobalData
   141	
   142	end Curve

   131	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
   132	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)

   136	      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega

   138

   140	/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
   141	common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
   142	theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
   143	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
   144	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
   145	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
   146	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   147	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
   148	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
   149	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
   150	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
   151	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
   152	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
   153	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
   154	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
   155	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
   156	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
   157	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
   158	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)
   159	
   160	end DivRepChartFamily
   161	
   162	/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/
   163	
   164	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
   165	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
   166	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
   167	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
   168	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
   169	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
   170	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   171	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
   172	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
   173	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   174	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
   175	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
   176	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   177	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
   178	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)
   179	
   180	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
   181	
   182	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
   183	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
   184	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
   185	noncomputable def equiv
   186	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   187	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
   188	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
   189	  toFun := D.pull S
   190	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
   191	  left_inv v :=
   192	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
   193	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
   194	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S
   195	
   196	@[simp]
   197	theorem equiv_apply
   198	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   199	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
   200	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   201	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
   202	  rfl
   203	
   204	@[simp]
   205	theorem equiv_symm_apply
   206	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   207	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
   208	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   209	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
   210	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
   211	  rfl
   212	
   213	/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
   214	theorem equiv_naturality
   215	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   216	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   217	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
   218	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
   219	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   220	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
   221	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi
   222	          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   223	            (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v) :=
   224	  D.pull_naturality phi v
   225	
   226	end DivRepAffinePullback

1	/-

     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: Christian Merten
     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
    66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc
    83	
    84	-- data
    85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
    89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
    93	
    94	-- data
    95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
    96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    99	  sorry
   100	
   101	namespace Jacobian
   102	
   103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
   104	
   105	-- data
   106	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
   107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
   108	  sorry
   109	
   110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
   111	genus of `C`. -/
   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
   113	  sorry
   114	
   115	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
   116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   121	  sorry
   122	
   123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
   124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
   125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
   126	  sorry
   127	
   128	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
   129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
   130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
   134	  sorry
   135	
   136	/--
   137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
   138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
   139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
   140	-/
   141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
   145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
   147	  sorry
   148	
   149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
   150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
   151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
   152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
   153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
   155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
   156	  map _ := sorry
   157	  map_id := sorry
   158	  map_comp := sorry
   159	
   160	end Jacobian
   161	
   162	/-! ## Base change of fields
   163	
   164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
   166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/

    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.

    42	## Notes

    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.

    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
    66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc
    83	
    84	-- data
    85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
    89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
    93	
    94	-- data
    95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
    96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    99	  sorry
   100	
   101	namespace Jacobian
   102	
   103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
   104	
   105	-- data
   106	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
   107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
   108	  sorry
   109	
   110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
   111	genus of `C`. -/
   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
   113	  sorry
   114	
   115	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
   116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   121	  sorry
   122	
   123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
   124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
   125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
   126	  sorry
   127	
   128	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
   129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
   130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
   134	  sorry
   135	
   136	/--
   137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
   138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
   139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
   140	-/
   141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
   145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
   147	  sorry
   148	
   149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
   150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
   151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
   152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
   153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
   155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
   156	  map _ := sorry
   157	  map_id := sorry
   158	  map_comp := sorry
   159	
   160	end Jacobian
   161	
   162	/-! ## Base change of fields
   163	
   164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
   166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0Functor
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
    10	
    11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
    12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
    13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
    14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
    15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
    16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
    17	
    18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
    19	
    20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
    21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
    22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
    23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
    24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
    25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
    26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
    27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
    28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
    29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
    30	
    31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
    32	
    33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
    35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
    36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
    37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
    38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
    39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
    40	
    41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
    42	
    43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
    44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
    45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
    46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
    47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
    48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
    49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
    50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
    51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
    52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
    53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
    54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
    55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
    61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
    63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
    65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
    66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
    67	-/
    68	
    69	set_option autoImplicit false
    70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    71	
    72	universe u
    73	
    74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    75	
    76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    77	
    78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    79	
    80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
    82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
    83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
    84	
    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
   101	
   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData
   147	
   148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
   149	registered)
   150	
   151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
   152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
   153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
   154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
   155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
   156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
   157	
   158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   159	
   160	open MonObj
   161	
   162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   164	
   165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
   166	elaborates with no transport. -/
   167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   168	
   169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
   170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
   171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
   172	defeq). -/
   173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
   174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
   177	
   178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
   179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
   180	scope). -/
   181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
   182	  inferInstance
   183	
   184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   185	
   186	end AlgebraicGeometry

   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);

   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:

   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=

    65	/-- The exact general-test data needed for the final F7 packaging.  In the intended

    68	structure DivRepGlobalData where

    70	    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
    71	  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    72	    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)
    73	  classify_pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver),

   127	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)

    87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
    88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
    89	bridge. -/
    90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
    91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
    92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
    93	  intro Y S hS
    94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
    95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
    96	  intro x hx
    97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
    98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
    99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
   100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
   101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
   102	        pullback.condition)
   103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
   104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
   105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
   106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
   107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
   108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
   109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
   110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
   111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
   112	    intro p
   113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
   114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
   115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
   116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
   118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
   119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
   120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
   121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
   122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
   123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
   124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
   125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
   126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
   127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
   128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
   129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
   130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
   131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
   132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
   133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
   134	    exact hs i
   135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
   136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'

   138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
   139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)

   141	      (ht' i)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.PiLocalization

/-! 
# The universal-family certificate assembly

This file assembles the seven fields of `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` from the
geometric inputs left by the universal-seed construction:

* finite chart colengths, supplied by the no-leak theorem in `SupportTubeFinite`;
* fibrewise regular chart equations, which make those colengths projective;
* a relative submodule spanning the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map;
* the fibre dimension of that kernel.

The last two inputs feed `SlicingFlatKernel`, simultaneously producing the projective
glued module, its constant rank, and both flat-cokernel clauses.  Keeping this assembly
generic isolates the remaining DD-4 geometry from the certificate bookkeeping.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)

omit [IsProper C.hom] in
/-- Assemble a divisor-family certificate from finite regular chart colengths and a
submodule which spans the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map.

The overlap product is kept as an explicit finite-flat input: producing it from the
universal seed is part of the geometric base-change wiring, while all consequences for
the certificate are discharged here. -/
theorem isCertified_of_kernel_spanning [IsNoetherianRing R] {n : Nat}
    (hfin : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
    (hregular : forall (j : A.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum R),
      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors
          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hovlFinite : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd)
    (hovlFlat : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd)
    (L : Submodule R A.chartProd)
    (hle : L <= LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
    (hspan : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) <=
        LinearMap.range (L.subtype.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hdim : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (LinearMap.ker
            ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = n) :
    A.IsCertified n := by
  letI hfiniteColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := hfin
  letI hprojectiveColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Projective R (A.colength j) :=
    fun j => A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hregular j)
  letI hflatColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) :=
    fun j => A.flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hregular j)
  letI hfiniteChart : Module.Finite R A.chartProd := Module.Finite.pi
  letI hflatChart : Module.Flat R A.chartProd := Module.Flat.pi_of_finite
  letI hfiniteOvl : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd := hovlFinite
  letI hflatOvl : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd := hovlFlat

    (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀))

end Curve

     8	/-!
     9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
    10	
    11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
    12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
    13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
    14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
    15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
    16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
    17	
    18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
    19	
    20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
    21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
    22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
    23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
    24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
    25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
    26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
    27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
    28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
    29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
    30	
    31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
    32	
    33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
    35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
    36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
    37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
    38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
    39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
    40	
    41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
    42	
    43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
    44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
    45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
    46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
    47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
    48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
    49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
    50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
    51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
    52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
    53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
    54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
    55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
    61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
    63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
    65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
    66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
    67	-/
    68	
    69	set_option autoImplicit false
    70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    71	
    72	universe u
    73	
    74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    75	
    76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    77	
    78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    79	
    80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
    82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
    83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
    84	
    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
   101	
   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData

   149	registered)

   151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
   152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis

   165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription

   167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj

   173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=

   184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests

     9	/-!
    10	# Conditional final packaging of divisor representability
    11	
    12	DDR-9.F7 has two logically separate parts: lifting the affine equivalences to arbitrary
    13	tests, and packaging the resulting natural equivalences as a `RepresentableBy` datum.
    14	This file formalizes the second part.  `DivRepGlobalData` records the general-test
    15	pullback, classification map, inverse laws, and naturality.  Its `representableBy`
    16	constructor is the final categorical packaging.
    17	
    18	The affine-to-general lift is intentionally not assumed to exist implicitly: a caller
    19	must provide every field of `DivRepGlobalData`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	set_option quotPrecheck false
    24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	open Grassmannian Scheme
    34	
    35	section Curve
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    38	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    39	
    40	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepKit :
    41	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    42	
    43	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    44	  [IsIntegral C.left]
    45	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    46	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
    47	  [IsDominant pi]
    48	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    49	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    50	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    51	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    52	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    53	variable (g r1 r2 : ℕ)
    54	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
    55	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    56	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
    57	  ↥(divisorSections k
    58	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    59	
    60	local notation "DivOver" =>
    61	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    62	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    63	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
    64	
    65	/-- The exact general-test data needed for the final F7 packaging.  In the intended
    66	construction, `pull` is assembled from the affine forward maps and `classify` by
    67	gluing the affine backward classifiers. -/
    68	structure DivRepGlobalData where
    69	  pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    70	    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
    71	  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    72	    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)
    73	  classify_pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
    74	    classify (pull v) = v
    75	  pull_classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T),
    76	    pull (classify F) = F
    77	  pull_comp : ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    78	    (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
    79	    pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (pull v)
    80	
    81	namespace DivRepGlobalData
    82	
    83	/-- The general-test equivalence underlying the represented functor. -/
    84	noncomputable def equiv
    85	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    86	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    87	    (T ⟶ DivOver) ≃ divFamZar C pi g T where
    88	  toFun := D.pull
    89	  invFun := D.classify
    90	  left_inv := D.classify_pull
    91	  right_inv := D.pull_classify
    92	
    93	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
    94	@[simp]
    95	theorem equiv_apply
    96	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    97	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
    98	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T v
    99	      = D.pull v :=
   100	  rfl
   101	
   102	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   103	@[simp]
   104	theorem equiv_symm_apply
   105	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
   106	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
   107	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T).symm F
   108	      = D.classify F :=
   109	  rfl
   110	
   111	/-- The final F7 categorical packaging: natural general-test pullback equivalences
   112	represent the locally certified divisor functor by `DivScheme`. -/
   113	noncomputable def representableBy
   114	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2) :
   115	    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver where
   116	  homEquiv {T} :=
   117	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T
   118	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
   119	    change D.pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (D.pull v)
   120	    exact D.pull_comp f v
   121	
   122	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   123	@[simp]
   124	theorem representableBy_homEquiv_apply
   125	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
   126	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
   127	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
   128	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv v = D.pull v :=
   129	  rfl
   130	
   131	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   132	@[simp]
   133	theorem representableBy_homEquiv_symm_apply
   134	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
   135	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
   136	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
   137	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv.symm F = D.classify F :=
   138	  rfl
   139	
   140	end DivRepGlobalData

   142	end Curve

    86	
    87	/-- Pull a supplied certified family on one carve chart to a test algebra and pass to
    88	the locally certified quotient.  This is the choice-free per-chart operation from which
    89	F5's affine forward map is glued. -/
    90	noncomputable def divRepPullAt
    91	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
    92	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    93	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    94	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    95	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
    96	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar
    97	
    98	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
    99	@[simp]
   100	theorem divRepPullAt_id
   101	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
   102	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
   103	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J) :
   104	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
   105	      = (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar :=
   106	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _
   107	
   108	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   109	/-- Pulling a chart family through two algebra maps is the same as pulling it through
   110	their composite.  This is the algebraic part of F5 naturality. -/
   111	theorem divRepPullAt_comp
   112	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
   113	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
   114	    {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]
   115	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
   116	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (phi : S →ₐ[k] T) :
   117	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
   118	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (phi.comp omega) :=
   119	  (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega phi (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar).symm
   120	
   121	namespace DivRepChartFamily
   122	
   123	/-- The precise F5 overlap obligation for a supplied family on every carve chart:
   124	two chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled locally
   125	certified divisor classes.  The future universal-family construction proves this from
   126	its epsilon identity and the total mono theorem. -/
   127	def IsCompatible
   128	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
   129	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
   130	  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   131	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
   132	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
   133	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),

   135	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
   136	      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
   137	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'
   138	
   139	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   140	/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
   141	common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
   142	theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
   143	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
   144	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
   145	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
   146	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   147	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
   148	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
   149	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
   150	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
   151	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
   152	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
   153	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
   154	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
   155	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :

   157	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
   158	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)
   159	
   160	end DivRepChartFamily
   161	
   162	/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/
   163	
   164	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
   165	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
   166	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
   167	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
   168	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
   169	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
   170	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   171	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
   172	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
   173	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   174	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
   175	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
   176	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   177	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
   178	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)
   179	
   180	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
   181	
   182	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
   183	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
   184	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
   185	noncomputable def equiv
   186	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   187	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
   188	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
   189	  toFun := D.pull S
   190	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
   191	  left_inv v :=
   192	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
   193	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
   194	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S
   195	
   196	@[simp]
   197	theorem equiv_apply
   198	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   199	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
   200	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   201	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
   202	  rfl
   203	
   204	@[simp]
   205	theorem equiv_symm_apply
   206	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   207	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
   208	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   209	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F

   211	  rfl
   212

   214	theorem equiv_naturality
   215	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   216	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   217	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
   218	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
   219	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   220	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
   221	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi
   222	          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)

    12	
    13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
    14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ

   136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'

   145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
   146	consumes. -/
   147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
   148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
   149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
   150	
   151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
   152	
   153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
   154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's

import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.PiLocalization
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SlicingFlatKernel
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SupportTubeFinite
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertOverlapFinite

/-! 
# The universal-family certificate assembly

This file assembles the seven fields of `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` from the
geometric inputs left by the universal-seed construction:

* finite chart colengths, supplied by the no-leak theorem in `SupportTubeFinite`;
* fibrewise regular chart equations, which make those colengths projective;
* a relative submodule spanning the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map;
* the fibre dimension of that kernel.

The last two inputs feed `SlicingFlatKernel`, simultaneously producing the projective
glued module, its constant rank, and both flat-cokernel clauses.  Keeping this assembly
generic isolates the remaining DD-4 geometry from the certificate bookkeeping.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)

omit [IsProper C.hom] in
/-- Assemble a divisor-family certificate from finite regular chart colengths and a
submodule which spans the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map.

The overlap product is kept as an explicit finite-flat input: producing it from the
universal seed is part of the geometric base-change wiring, while all consequences for
the certificate are discharged here. -/
theorem isCertified_of_kernel_spanning [IsNoetherianRing R] {n : Nat}
    (hfin : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
    (hregular : forall (j : A.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum R),
      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors
          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hovlFinite : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd)
    (hovlFlat : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd)
    (L : Submodule R A.chartProd)
    (hle : L <= LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
    (hspan : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) <=
        LinearMap.range (L.subtype.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hdim : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (LinearMap.ker
            ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = n) :
    A.IsCertified n := by
  letI hfiniteColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := hfin

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]

noncomputable local instance instOverCleftRepClassifyZar :
    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [IsIntegral C.left]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [IsDominant π]

variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
